column1: # Palestine, PA Dar al-Iftaa: the perpetual al-Aqsa Mosque table, printed on the perpetual winter
# (standard) clock all year -- UTC+02:00 fixed, never the summer clock -- hence `clock` differs from
# `zone` (Asia/Hebron or Asia/Gaza, the engine's own civil zones, which do observe DST).
# Ruling R118 (owner, 2 Oct 2026): the authority's own printed town offsets apply to its al-Aqsa table.
# The whole table (366 days, every printed time) read from the two prints held, the 2012 printing and
# the 2026 yearly calendar's reprint, identical on every cell (archive/tables/manual/ps-iftaa/2026-10-02/,
# with the printed offset list, offsets.tsv); each town's table is the al-Aqsa table plus its printed
# offset on every time alike, for every Palestinian town of the list: Jerusalem, Ramallah, Bethlehem,
# Jenin, Nablus + 0; Jericho - 1; Hebron, Idhna, Dura, Beit Awwa, Tulkarm + 1; Qalqilya + 1.5; Gaza + 3;
# Rafah, Khan Yunis, Deir al-Balah + 4; and the list's towns in Israel (review r2 of R118), units only so that a place in
# Palestine nearer one of them takes its figure: Nazareth, Umm al-Fahm + 0; Tiberias, Safed, Beisan - 1; Haifa, Acre,
# Kafr Qasim, Tayibe + 1; Lydd, Ramla + 1.5 (starts + 2, ends + 1, as Qalqilya); Beersheba, Jaffa + 2 (points approximate,
# zone Asia/Jerusalem). Each town is a unit at its own point (the app's city point;
# Beit Awwa's approximate point, not in the app's cities), whose table is al-Aqsa's computed times plus the printed
# minutes (Levant.paTowns): each row names its unit, and the gate checks the point resolves to it.
# Qalqilya's minute and a half: two derived tables, + 2 for its starts (a whole minute never before the
# half-minute instant) and + 1 for its ends (never after it), each row checking only those columns.
# The PA prints no imsak: its Fajr is when the fast begins, so every Fajr column is `F+E` (the end of
# eating never after the printed Fajr).
# Split, forward in time: fit on al-Aqsa's table on its printing year, 2012 (a leap year: every printed
# line, 29 February included), and on 2026 (the 2026 calendar's own print); held out, al-Aqsa's table
# mapped onto 2027 (no 2027 calendar yet), six dates of the Ramadan 1447 (2026) imsakiya (a third print),
# and every town's table (nothing is fitted at a town: its times are al-Aqsa's plus its printed minutes).
# 2027 held out was early by 1 min on a few days of Fajr, sunrise, Maghrib and Isha at al-Aqsa (a
# perpetual table against the leap cycle): those margins are widened to the three years' bound
# (Levant.kt). Class D (ruling R57): never early, at most 3 min late at every town, no exception.
